newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Minor Australian ruling party rejects land deal.
newsitem.headline: Minor Australian ruling party rejects land deal.

text.p: The junior party in Australia's ruling Liberal-National coalition on Tuesday rejected Prime Minister John Howard's planned solution to a bitter land rights row between Aborigines and farmers.
The National Party called for Howard's compromise strategy to be changed to wipe out Aboriginal native title rights to land leased to farmers.

The Nationals said "...the grant of a pastoral lease is to be regarded as having extinguished native title..." and that the party's parliamentarians must push for reforms to Howard's plan, even to the unusual step of seeking amendments in parliament.
The Nationals have consistently said the extinguishment of native title is the only way to give farmers certainty over the use of the land they have leased from the government.

Howard, who is also facing opposition from his own Liberal Party, has refused to extinguish native title. Howard says up to 78 percent of Australia's 7.68 million square kms (2.96 million square miles) could be affected by native title claims.
Last Thursday, Howard released his 10-point native title plan, which he says gives farmers security over their leases while recognising Aboriginal traditional rights.

In addition to setting out rights for farmers and Aborigines, the plan also reduces Aboriginal rights to negotiate over development and other uses of land and exempts cities, towns and water catchments from Aboriginal claims.
Aborigines say the plan effectively wipes-out native title.

Native title laws were introduced by the former Labor government three years ago, but became an urgent political issue when the High Court decided last December that land leased to farmers for generations could be liable to Aboriginal claim.
